measurements.verbatim_quote: In total, 11 out of 335 subjects (3.3%) experienced a thrombotic event in the fitusiran clinical development program. Of the subjects who experienced thrombotic events, 7 out 270 subjects (2.6%) had a thrombotic event while receiving the original 80-mg dose regimen and 4 out of 286 (1.4%) subjects had a thrombotic event on the AT-DR. No subjects in the on-demand (control) arms in the randomized controlled trials (studies EFC14768 and EFC14769) experienced a thrombotic event.
measurements.notes: ON-TARGET pharmacology taken too far: fitusiran is designed to lower antithrombin and raise thrombin generation, so thrombosis is excessive pharmacologic effect rather than an off-target chemistry effect. FDA required a Boxed Warning for thromboembolism. Source spells '7 out 270' (missing 'of') - reproduced verbatim.

extraction_notes:
SCOPE. Bundle z-human-fda-reviews-a, human data only. All 93 measurement rows are human (species=human, study_type=clinical); no animal row was carried over even where the same document contains extensive monkey/mouse coagulation data (fitusiran monkey D-dimer/AT tables, imetelstat monkey aPTT tables, olezarsen monkey APTT). Those belong to the animal side of the dataset and were deliberately left out of this file.

QUOTE FIDELITY. Every verbatim_quote was machine-verified against the whitespace-normalised source text before this file was written (93/93 matched). The source .txt files are PDF-to-text conversions in which table cells land on separate lines, so a quoted table row is the concatenation of consecutive cell lines with single spaces; nothing else was altered. Curly quotes, en-dashes and the source's own typos were preserved (e.g. fitusiran '7 out 270 subjects', olezarsen 'there was no meaningful differences were noted', 'EFC151110' in the Table 148 caption, imetelstat 'groop').

FIGURE DISCIPLINE. No number in this file was read off a plotted panel. Fitusiran's dose-AT relationship (Figures 2, 3, 22, 29, 30), thrombin generation over time (Figures 31, 32), ABR by AT quartile (Figure 4), ABR vs averaged AT (Figures 45, 46) and olezarsen's platelet-over-time plots (Figures 11-13) are all figures; where the only content was a figure, the row carries readout_value NOT_REPORTED with readout_is_qualitative true. Fitusiran Table 8 ('Efficacy and Mean AT Levels of the 80 mg QM Regimen in Three Parent Phase 3 Studies') is an embedded slide image with NO extractable text in the conversion - its numbers are absent from this file for that reason.

CONTRADICTIONS FOUND IN THE SOURCES (all recorded, none reconciled):
1. Imetelstat aPTT, within NDA 217779: the narrative on review p.281 says 'Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (PTT) was seen in 22% of patients in the imetelstat arm, including two who had grade 3 prolongations', while Table 77 on the next page gives 26% with 1.0% grade 3-4 and Table 86 gives 25/98 (26%) with one grade 3. Both the 22% claim and the 26% tables are carried as separate rows and flagged.
2. Imetelstat coagulation, sponsor vs regulator, within NDA 217779: under 'The Applicant's Position' the sponsor wrote 'Coagulation Not applicable.'; FDA replied 'We do not agree with the assessment above, which underestimates the significance and extent of cytopenias, coagulation abnormalities, and hepatic function abnormalities'. A miner who trusted sponsor text alone would record a false absence for the one compound in this bundle with a real human aPTT signal.
3. Fitusiran Pool C ABR, within NDA 219019: the narrative says the AT-DR ABR was '5.7 (95% CI: 3.9, 8.2)', Table 148 prints '5.6 (3.9, 8.2)', and the FDA statistical team's own re-derivation gives '5.8 (4.0, 8.4)'. All three are recorded.
4. Fitusiran thrombotic-event counts, within NDA 219019: Section 7.6.1 counts 4 thrombotic events on the AT-DR (4/286), while the AT-DR TEAE table (Table 44) shows only 2 (0.7%) thrombosis events. The difference is a definitional artefact stated in the table footnote - 'AEs were not considered treatment-emergent if they occurred during the follow-up after a subject's AT value was 60% or greater' - and both numbers are carried.
5. Tofersen thrombosis, within NDA 215887: the SAE table (Table 22) shows 5.6% vs 2.8% (an apparent excess), while the all-TEAE table (Table 27) shows 5.6% vs 5.6% (no difference at all). Both are recorded; the second is the honest counterweight to the first.
6. Tofersen coagulation shift rates, within EMA/276404/2024: INR shifts differ between arms (31.3% vs 19.4%) while raw PT shifts do not (50.0% vs 51.9%), even though INR is a transform of PT. EMA itself explains the whole pattern as a central-laboratory reference-range problem that triggered corrective actions - the very high absolute shift rates in BOTH arms are an assay artefact, not a drug effect. Anyone using the tofersen coagulation numbers must carry that caveat.

DATA GAPS THAT MUST NOT BE READ AS NULLS. Three rows record cells that look like zeros but are missing data: olezarsen Trial CS3 Table 51 lists 'PT, high (sec) Missing NA NA NA NA NA'; eplontersen Trial ION-682884-CS3 Table 50 lists PT as '0/0 (NA)' for BOTH the eplontersen and inotersen arms while the external placebo cohort has PT data. And fitusiran NDA 219019 has NO clinical clotting-time data at all - its human safety laboratory table (Table 45) contains only chemistry analytes; the single human D-dimer statement ('Increases in fibrin D-Dimer have been reported in clinical studies with fitusiran') is buried in the monkey toxicology narrative and carries no number, timepoint or denominator. Those are regulatory/reporting silences, recorded as such.

ON-TARGET vs UNINTENDED. Fitusiran is the only compound here whose coagulation effect is the intended pharmacology: its antithrombin lowering, thrombin-generation rise and ABR reduction are on_target_effect=true, and its thrombotic events are flagged BOTH on-target (excessive pharmacology) and unintended toxicity - FDA required a Boxed Warning for thromboembolism and a companion diagnostic for AT activity. Imetelstat's aPTT/PT prolongation is the classic phosphorothioate/oligonucleotide-class intrinsic-pathway effect and is flagged unintended only. Bleeding in the hemophilia population is the underlying disease, so fitusiran's haemorrhage AE rows are flagged neither on-target nor unintended, per FDA's own attribution.

PLATELET RULE. Only two platelet-linked rows are included (imetelstat Applicant Table 95; olezarsen Section 7.7.2), both with readout_category platelet_coag_crosstalk, and only because the source itself pairs the platelet count with a bleeding outcome inside the same analysis. Bare platelet counts and thrombocytopenia incidences - which are abundant in the imetelstat, olezarsen, eplontersen and tofersen reviews - were left to the separate thrombocytopenia endpoint.

CROSS-COMPOUND COMPARISONS THIS BUNDLE MAKES POSSIBLE. (a) Same sequence, different chemistry, randomized head-to-head in humans: eplontersen (GalNAc, mixed PO/PS, 45 mg monthly SC) vs inotersen (unconjugated, full PS, 300 mg weekly SC) in Trial ION-682884-CS3 - haemorrhage-related AEs 9.7% vs 29.2%, risk difference -19.4 (-38.3, -0.6). (b) Same sequence, different chemistry, across programmes: olezarsen (GalNAc) shows no clinical bleeding signal at all, while its unconjugated parent volanesorsen showed 36% vs 6% clinical bleeding events. (c) Route matters: tofersen is dosed intrathecally and shows essentially no systemic coagulation signal, whereas IV imetelstat at 7.1 mg/kg shows a 26% aPTT prolongation rate.

SEQUENCE AND PER-POSITION CHEMISTRY. Sequences were NOT available in any of the five FDA reviews; all three published sequences come from the EMA assessment reports (tofersen shorthand with an explicit legend in EMA/276404/2024 p.14; olezarsen and imetelstat as full IUPAC/CAS chemical names in EMA/277774/2025 p.12 and EMA/13310/2025 p.14). Modification rows are written only for those three. Fitusiran, eplontersen, inotersen and volanesorsen get an EMPTY per-position record because no source in this bundle publishes their bases - fitusiran's review states only that antisense strand A-116861 has a '19-mer core sequence' without printing it, and eplontersen's states only that it is a 20-mer with 'the same nucleotide sequence as inotersen'. Rendering convention: both EMA chemical names distinguish deoxythymidine (T) from 2'-MOE 5-methyluridine (MeU / m5rU); nucleobase and sequence_base render both as T because 5-methyluracil is thymine, and each modification row's basis states which residue the source actually printed. Imetelstat's 3'-amino-3'-deoxyribose has no matching sugar_mod enum value, so it is recorded as DNA (for the 2'-deoxy sugar) with the 3'-amino substitution carried by backbone_linkage_3p = PN and spelled out in every basis string.

LICENSING NUANCE. S1-S5 are US FDA review documents and are true public-domain US Government works. S6-S8 are EMA assessment reports; EMA asserts copyright with the standing permission 'Reproduction is authorised provided the source is acknowledged'. They are recorded as redistribution 'public_domain' per the bundle instruction, but that is a simplification - downstream users should acknowledge EMA as the source rather than treat these three as unencumbered.

DENOMINATOR HAZARD IN THE EMA OLEZARSEN REPORT. EMA/277774/2025 Table 42 (Pool 1) survives PDF-to-text conversion with its column headers shattered across lines ('50 m / g / (N = / 21)'). The per-study CS3 and CS8 cells are internally arithmetically consistent, but the pooled Pool 1 column values do not reproduce their stated denominators (e.g. '6 (8.9)' against a stated N=62, where 6/62 = 9.7%). Pool 1 was therefore NOT extracted; the Pool 4 table, whose columns do reproduce, was extracted instead.

Every one of them is an image in the PDF-to-text conversion. Refused: reading a value off a plotted panel is explicitly forbidden and would have been undetectable in review.

2. FITUSIRAN TABLE 8. 'Efficacy and Mean AT Levels of the 80 mg QM Regimen in Three Parent Phase 3 Studies' is a pasted applicant slide; the caption and abbreviations survive the conversion but the cells do not. The surrounding prose says only that 'the mean AT levels are close to 10% with fitusiran treatment', which is a characterisation rather than a value. Refused rather than guessing the cells.

3. EMA OLEZARSEN POOL 1 BLEEDING COLUMN (EMA/277774/2025 Table 42). Looked extractable - it is plain text with numbers - but the pooled percentages do not reconcile with the printed denominators after the column headers were mangled by the text conversion ('6 (8.9)' with a stated N=62 implies 9.7%). Refused the pooled column; extracted the internally consistent per-study columns from the FDA review (Table 70) and the Pool 4 table instead.

4. ALL ANIMAL COAGULATION DATA IN THESE FILES. NDA 219019 alone contains monkey mean-percent D-dimer, AT protein, AT activity and thrombin-generation-peak tables (Tables 79-81, 92-95), a hemophilia-A-mouse aPTT table (Table 59, Table 99) and dog/rat findings; NDA 217779 and EMA/13310/2025 contain monkey aPTT and prothrombin-time ranges (e.g. 'aPTT (s) 16.8 - 17.4 19.1 - 19.9 ... 17.9 - 51.0 19.2 - 40.1'); NDA 218614 contains a monkey APTT prolongation up to 1.5x baseline at 30 mg/kg/wk. All in scope for the project but out of scope for a HUMAN-only round, and this round exists specifically to correct a 1,476-animal / 886-human imbalance. Not extracted here.

5. BARE PLATELET COUNTS AND THROMBOCYTOPENIA RATES. Imetelstat (platelets decreased 97% all-grade / 65% grade 3-4 vs 34% / 8% placebo; Table 85 by cycle), olezarsen (Table 51 platelet thresholds; mean baselines 200/188/215 x10^9/L), tofersen and eplontersen all have rich platelet data. Refused because platelet count alone is a different endpoint with its own dossier; only the two rows where the source itself ties platelets to a bleeding outcome were taken.

6. FITUSIRAN INDIVIDUAL SUBJECT IDENTIFIERS. Table 51 and the SAE narratives are partly redacted ((b) (6)) so subject identity, exact ages and study assignment are incomplete. I used the diagnosis/age label exactly as printed (e.g. 'HBwI/17') and did not attempt to match narratives to table rows across sections, which would have required inference.

7. IMETELSTAT INDIVIDUAL DEATH NARRATIVES. Several are bleeding or thrombotic deaths (fatal GI haemorrhage on day 25 with a normal platelet count and 'Coagulation profile was not documented'; a fatal mesenteric-vessel thrombosis on day 953; a sudden death where the reviewer wrote 'an acute intracranial hemorrhage cannot be ruled out'). I did not create measurement rows for these because in each case the coagulation status at the event was explicitly undocumented or the attribution was speculative; forcing them into rows would have manufactured signal. They are named here so a reviewer can find them.

8. LABEL-DERIVED AND SECONDARY-CITATION NUMBERS. The fitusiran review quotes emicizumab, marstacimab and concizumab thrombotic-risk language from other products' USPIs, and the olezarsen review quotes the volanesorsen 36%/6% bleeding comparison from EMDAC 2018. Only the volanesorsen figure was taken (flagged in its notes as a secondary citation without denominators, kept because it is the direct unconjugated comparator for olezarsen); the other products' label statements were refused because they are neither oligonucleotides nor original analyses in these documents.

9. FITUSIRAN 'AT ACTIVITY 15-35%' TARGET WINDOW. It appears dozens of times across NDA 219019 but it is a dosing rule, not a measurement. Only the actually measured AT levels (mean 23.5% (4.64%) in LTE15174, the per-study percent-of-baseline values, and the eleven per-subject AT levels at the time of a thrombotic event) were extracted.
